title: config: disable DTLS 0.9 and 1.0 system-wide
commit_message:
config: disable DTLS 0.9 and 1.0 system-wide

Ubuntu has decided to disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 system-wide several years
ago. I recently found out that the existing change in gnutls was not
sufficient to really achieve that and fixed it through the system
configuration file. While doing so, I found out that this only applied
to TLS and not DTLS but didn't want to reword my change back then due to
unrelated issues in the archive which were going on at the same time.

This commit disables DTLS 0.9 and 1.0 in the same way than TLS 1.0 and
1.1 have been disabled.

For context, there are several versions versions of DTLS: 1.0, 1.2, 1.3.
No 0.9 and no 1.1. DTLS 0.9 seems to be similar to a draft of DTLS 1.0,
and DTLS 1.0 is based on TLS 1.1. Starting with DTLS 1.2, version
numbers match TLS version numbers.

The biggest user of DTLS 0.9 and 1.0 is probably OpenConnect. However
the maintainers consider that the support of these protocols is a key
requirement for their software and its compatibility with outdated
network equipments which can only handle these DTLS versions in
hardware. They have thus "opted out" of the system configuration after
similar changes in Fedora and will therefore be unaffected.
diff:
diff --git a/debian/changelog b/debian/changelog
index 856fd4d..5a574ed 100644
--- a/debian/changelog
+++ b/debian/changelog
@@ -1,3 +1,9 @@
+gnutls28 (3.8.1-4ubuntu7) noble; urgency=medium
+
+  * Forcefully disable DTLS 0.9 and 1.0 through /etc/gnutls/config.
+
+ -- Adrien Nader <adrien.nader@canonical.com>  Wed, 03 Jan 2024 15:06:38 +0100
+
 gnutls28 (3.8.1-4ubuntu6) noble; urgency=medium
 
   * SECURITY UPDATE: timing side-channel inside RSA-PSK key exchange
diff --git a/debian/conf/config b/debian/conf/config
index 447fe0c..a545960 100644
--- a/debian/conf/config
+++ b/debian/conf/config
@@ -1,4 +1,6 @@
 [overrides]
 disabled-version = tls1.0
 disabled-version = tls1.1
+disabled-version = dtls0.9
+disabled-version = dtls1.0
